{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The Republican vision for American banking calls for establishing transparent, efficient markets where consumers can obtain loans they need at reasonable rates based on market conditions.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Democratic-controlled Congress enacted the Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, otherwise known as Dodd-Frank, in response to the financial institutions crisis of 2008-2009.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act did not let the financial crisis of 2008-2009 go to waste but used it as an excuse to establish unprecedented government control over the nation's financial markets.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The consequences of the Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act have been bad for everyone except federal regulators.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act did not address the cause of the financial crisis of 2008-2009, which was the government's own housing policies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act extended government control over the economy by creating new unaccountable bureaucracies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Central planning of the financial sector has not created jobs, but has killed them.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Central planning of the financial sector has not limited risks, but has created more.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Central planning of the financial sector has not encouraged economic growth, but has shackled it.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
